claim: Frasers Group, the one proven 2025-26 buyer of Continental sports-retail store estates, agreed in Nov-2025 to buy Hervis's entire Hungarian (29 stores) and Romanian (49 stores) businesses, staff included, subject to competition approval. Hervis said it was exiting fashion-oriented markets. Frasers' capital is also heavily committed elsewhere: it now holds about 47.89% of Hugo Boss after its takeover offer (final results 18-Aug-2026), and it announced the acquisition of Harvey Nichols on 13-Aug-2026. No Frasers RNS mentions Foot Locker.
data_point: Hervis HU 29 + RO 49 = 78 stores transferred with employees, price undisclosed (announced ~25-Nov-2025). Hugo Boss offer: 12,157,598 shares (~17.62%) tendered; Frasers total 33,054,959 shares (~47.89%); EC merger clearance 27-Jul-2026. Frasers RNS 13-Aug-2026: 'Frasers Group Acquisition of Harvey Nichols'.
source_name: Daily News Hungary (2025-11-27); HUGO BOSS IR press release (2026-08-18); Investegate Frasers RNS list
original_quote: all 29 Hungarian stores and 49 Romanian outlets - along with their employees - will be transferred to Frasers Group once competition authorities in both countries approve the deal
verifier_note: Verified directly: the DNH article (datePublished 2025-11-27) and the Hugo Boss IR release https://group.hugoboss.com/en/newsroom/news/news-detail/hugo-boss-notes-results-of-voluntary-public-takeover-offer-by-frasers-group-1 (47.89%, 12,157,598 shares, 17.62%). The Investegate FRAS list shows the Harvey Nichols RNS (13-Aug-2026). The scraper's '>75 stores' is correct (78). Not verified: the Hervis Austria sale to a Snipes-founder consortium and the 17-of-93 closures. The Maxi Sport / 'launch Sports Direct in Italy' part is a DUPLICATE of D_w1_sector-backdrop #14 and is excluded here. Downgraded A->B because nothing here concerns FL directly. The read-across is inference: a sale of a whole country estate with staff to a consolidator is a live 2025-26 CEE exit template (alongside JD->Sport Vision franchising), but Frasers' balance sheet is absorbed by Hugo Boss, Harvey Nichols and Accent.

claim: Fourlis, FL's licensee in SE Europe, said on its H1-2026 call that seven new Foot Locker stores had been opened to date. Its Sporting Goods segment posted an EBIT of minus EUR0.7m on revenue up 14.2% to EUR109.5m, a loss it attributed to Foot Locker expansion costs, Romania challenges and stock rationalisation. The licensee is still expanding the FL banner, but the rollout is loss-making in the ramp phase.
data_point: Seven new FL stores opened to date (2026). Sporting Goods revenue EUR109.5m (+14.2%), EBIT -EUR0.7m. Group one-off network rationalisation cost EUR1.6m in H1, mainly Romania. Per Edison: plan of 8-10 FL openings a year; break-even in year 1, ~5% in year 2, 8-10% when mature.
source_name: Fourlis H1-2026 earnings call highlights (GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance); Edison Group
original_quote: Sporting Goods EBIT: Minus EUR0.7 million, reflecting Foot Locker expansion costs, Romania challenges, and stock rationalization. ... Foot Locker Expansion: Seven new stores opened up to date.
verifier_note: Verified the Yahoo/GuruFocus page directly (curl). It is a call summary, not a transcript, hence tier B. The '1-2 underperforming Foot Locker stores under evaluation' (Romania) part is a DUPLICATE of D_w1_sector-backdrop #11 (MoneyBuzz 2026-09-13), as are the Edison store economics, so only the 7-openings and segment-loss data are new. Correction to the scraper: 'seven ... to date' most likely refers to 2026 openings, not ~17 months. The FL licensee base was ~13 at 31-Dec-2025 per the scrape's licensing-template notes, against a 2026 plan of 10 Greece + 2 Bulgaria, so the licensee is roughly on its plan. That cuts against the scraper's 'below plan' framing. The point that a licensee absorbs only a handful of stores a year still stands.

claim: Laura Lopez, FL's Iberia VP, gave Modaes an on-record interview after the deal (31-Oct-2025). She said Iberia is one of FL's European 'big six' markets with about 60 stores, and Iberia plus France about 217. New openings depend on the global budget, but 'a list is ready' of strategic cities. She also said DKS plans, for now, are to strengthen Foot Locker in Europe rather than bring the DICK'S brand there.
data_point: Iberia ~60 stores (~800 staff); Iberia+France 217. The implied France figure of ~157 does not match the other counts: FR locator 140-142 and SIRENE 145 active establishments (Oct-2026), or ~149 on the locator at deal close, so treat the 217 as approximate. Current locator ES 46-48 + PT 9-11 = ~55-59.
original_quote: Dependera del presupuesto global que se destine, pero tenemos preparada una lista por ciudades y mercados estrategicos
english_translation: It will depend on the global budget allocated, but we have a list ready of strategic cities and markets
verifier_note: The article page returns 403 to WebFetch and curl, and the search and Apify quotas are exhausted. A Modaes listing page cached in the scratchpad confirms the headline, the author (Celia Oliveras), the date (31 oct 2025) and the teaser naming 'Laura Lopez, vicepresidenta del negocio en el territorio', who says there is 'gran margen de crecimiento ... al calor del musculo de Dick's'. The 60/217 counts and the 'lista' quote were not seen directly. An independent scraper (raw/B_w1_registry-italy-iberia.md) reports the same figures. Not in KNOWN_BRIEF, the baseline or any confirmed file. Note that ~Oct-2025 Iberia/France counts are later contradicted by post-deal closures in Spain (Barakaldo, Armilla, Vitoria) and France.

claim: JD Sports chose a capital-light franchise to enter Mexico rather than buying a store estate (RNS 4392V, 21-Sep-2026). From 2027 Grupo Axo will operate more than 140 JD premises using its existing sneaker-store estate. JD says JD and Courir already have 75 franchise stores across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
data_point: Axo to operate >140 JD premises from 2027 by converting its existing sneaker stores; 75 JD/Courir franchise stores; 83 franchised stores in a further 15 countries; JD has 4,766 stores. No mention of Foot Locker.
original_quote: JD and Courir currently have 75 franchise stores across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia, supporting the Group's ambition to expand into attractive new markets through partnerships under a proven model with best-in-class local operators.
verifier_note: Verified on jdplc.com (HTTP 200 via curl). The quote, date, RNS number, '>140' and 'commencing in 2027' are all there. Downgraded A->C because it is only indirect evidence on JD's appetite to buy FL's ~559 owned European stores. JD's capital-light preference is already implied by the confirmed JD/Sport Vision CEE franchise items (D_w1_sector-backdrop #1-2). The '£260m returned' figure was not checked.

claim: JD is consolidating Greek sports retail, where FL is licensed to Fourlis. Via its 100% unit Cosmos Sport, JD notified the Hellenic Competition Commission on 2-Oct-2026 of its acquisition of 100% of Sport Vision Greece (20 stores) from BDS Sport Group, so FL's licensee now faces a larger JD-led rival.
data_point: Cosmos Sport FY to 31-Jan-2026: sales EUR212.2m (+16.1%), EBITDA EUR39.45m, PBT EUR20m, >99 stores in GR/CY. Sport Vision Greece: 10 Sport Vision, 9 Buzz and 1 Tike stores; capital increase of EUR12.8m on 18-Aug-2026. Convert Group Big-3 sell-out Jan-Aug 2026: EUR344.6m incl. VAT (+16.3%). Fourlis sports Jan-Aug: +12%, LFL +8%.
original_quote: Η συναλλαγή, η οποία θα πραγματοποιηθεί μέσω της Cosmos Sport, γνωστοποιήθηκε στις 2 Οκτωβρίου στην Επιτροπή Ανταγωνισμού και αφορά την απόκτηση του 100% του μετοχικού κεφαλαίου της Sport Vision Μονοπρόσωπη Α.Ε.
english_translation: The transaction, to be carried out via Cosmos Sport, was notified on 2 October to the Competition Commission and concerns the acquisition of 100% of the share capital of Sport Vision Single-Member S.A.
verifier_note: Verified the capital.gr article directly (curl, page dated Wednesday 07-Oct-2026 07:30). Every quoted figure was found. The byline name was not found in the extracted text. The '1-2 Foot Locker stores under evaluation in Romania' sentence is present but is a DUPLICATE of D_w1_sector-backdrop #11. Downgraded B->C: this is competitor consolidation in a licensed market and has no direct bearing on a DKS exit of owned FL Europe/APAC stores. The Romania Sport Vision/MIG deal is already in D_w1_sector-backdrop #10; the Greece deal is new.

claim: The Frasers bid for Accent Group (A$0.65 per share, unconditional, from a 22.9% stake) was unanimously rejected by Accent's board as materially inadequate (24-Jun-2026). The offer period has reportedly been extended a second time, to 29-Jan-2027. ANZ sneaker retail, FL APAC's core, therefore remains in play, with Frasers creeping toward control of FL's main ANZ rival.
data_point: Board rejection 2026-06-24 (SGI Europe). First extension, to 30-Sep-2026, was announced 23-Jul-2026 (Frasers RNS). The second extension to 29-Jan-2027 is reported by Kalkine (2026-09-18) only.
source_name: SGI Europe; Frasers RNS via Investegate; Kalkine
original_quote: Accent Group's board unanimously rejects Frasers' offer of A$0.65 per share, calling it materially inadequate.
verifier_note: The offer, its price and the first extension to 30-Sep-2026 are a DUPLICATE of D_w1_sector-backdrop #9, so only the rejection and the Jan-2027 extension are incremental. The SGI rejection was verified (2026-06-24). Kalkine returns 403. Investegate's FRAS RNS list (to 05-Oct-2026) shows no second 'Update on Offer for Accent', so the Jan-2027 extension may have been an ASX-only bidder notice; it is unverified, hence PLAUSIBLE. Downgraded A->C: it is relevant to FL APAC only by inference, as no source links Frasers/Accent to Foot Locker.

data_point: Store 94832, Shop 1089/1 Westfield Miranda, 600 The Kingsway, is live on stores.footlocker.com.au (HTTP 200, 2026-10-07). The re-opening date of 24-Sep-2026 comes from Instagram only.
